evidence.supports: Full conditional duration clause, including whichever sooner and council termination requirement.
evidence.quote:
Section 4. Duration of Moratorium. The moratorium imposed by this ordinance shall

commence on the date of the adoption of this ordinance. As long as the Town holds a public

hearing on the moratorium and adopts findings and conclusions in support of the moratorium

(as contemplated by Section 5 herein), the moratorium shall not terminate until six (6) months

after the date of adoption, or at the time all of the tasks described herein have been

accomplished, whichever is sooner. The Council shall make the decision to terminate the

moratorium by ordinance, and termination shall not otherwise be presumed to have occurred.
moratorium on the acceptance, processing, or approval of any applications for permits or land

decisions.notes: Section 4 conditions its duration language on the public hearing and findings; later hearing and current force remain unverified.

duration.from: Six months minimum; by its own terms the moratorium does not terminate until the Council, following the required public hearing, adopts findings and either extends or cancels it -- termination is not presumed to occur merely because six months have elapsed
duration.to: The ordinance imposes an immediate six-month moratorium. Subject to its hearing and findings condition, section 4 refers to six months after adoption or completion of the listed tasks, whichever is sooner; the Council decides termination by ordinance and termination is not otherwise presumed.
duration.reason: Section 4 does not establish a six-month minimum.

duration_days.reason: The ordinance uses calendar months and an earlier event.

duration_kind.reason: Section 4 provides for completion of tasks or six months, whichever is sooner, subject to its stated conditions.

evidence.quote:
B. Public Hearing and Approval of Ordinance – Data Center Moratorium:

Mr. Rogerson presented Ordinance 3946 that, if approved, will ratify

and confirm the moratorium on the acceptance of applications for

permits for data centers  for an additional six months.

Mayor Donovan opened the public hearing. Hearing no

comments, Mayor Donovan closed the public hearing.

Council will continue discussions of next steps at an upcoming

Committee meeting.

Councilmember Hudson moved to continue the

moratorium on the acceptance of applications for

permits for data centers with the adoption of

Ordinance 3946. Motion seconded by

Councilmember Tercero.  Motion passed 7-0.

decisions.notes: Minutes describe an additional six months, while packet ordinance text anchors a six-month maximum to Ordinance 3943; the code index lists March 23, 2027. Signed text and reconciliation of these conflicts, later action, and current force remain unresolved. No end date is asserted.
